answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit that grows with every identity it claims, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits. New identities start with near-zero trust and earn weight only through slow, verified work, like a zephyr that can only bend the trellis over time, not snap it. When a fake cluster is caught, its whole deposit is slashed and its reputation tide turns, wiping the attacker's sunk cost while honest agents keep earning.
